conf.description: AWS GovCloud CloudTrail console-signin / eventbridge direct route: strip the EventBridge envelope, scrub the HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS sentinel username BEFORE it is indexed OR re-serialized, then restore the scrubbed record to _raw, per recommendations.direct.cribl - overrides the field table's aws.cloudtrail.flattened.detail custom target the same way management-events does, but scrub-before-snapshot instead of snapshot-before-mutate because this dataset's own security note requires it

conf.comment: EventBridge delivers one console sign-in record per message under detail{}. This is the lowest-volume, highest-value dataset (per description) so detail is kept as _raw like management-events - but userIdentity.userName can carry HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS on a failed sign-in, which the field notes say 'can contain a password a user typed into the wrong box' and 'must be scrubbed rather than indexed'. So the scrub runs on the nested detail object BEFORE the _raw snapshot, unlike management-events which snapshots first - here fidelity loses to the explicit security instruction for this one field.

functions.description: Pipeline purpose and why the scrub-then-snapshot order differs from the sibling management-events pipeline
Parse the EventBridge envelope and native console sign-in record under detail{} from _raw JSON

Scrub the sentinel username IN the nested detail object first (statement form, not a single eval expression, since it needs an if-block), then snapshot the now-scrubbed record into _raw - the mask function's fields[] path-addressing on a nested key is unverified against this instance, so code (proven-safe __e bracket/dot access) is used instead

Computed fields read from ORIGINAL vendor names before rename: 'detail-type' bracket access (hyphen); event.outcome lowercased from the responseElements key matching eventName (ConsoleLogin), per the field notes' 'authoritative outcome read from the responseElements key matching eventName'; MFAUsed Yes/No string to boolean; user.name deliberately omitted (left undefined, i.e. NOT indexed) rather than set to the sentinel literal - the code step above already scrubbed the copy going to _raw, this is the copy going to the ECS field
_time from the in-record sign-in-attempt time (genuinely nested path) - never @timestamp
Batch rename of the clean envelope field and the clean nested detail.eventName ECS anchor
event.dataset (no hyphen) and cleanup of the now-partially-mutated 'detail' object (superseded by the scrubbed _raw snapshot above) and the hyphenated envelope key via glob
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
